attacked.target: The receipt of 400 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The valuation date is the date of receipt (2026-06-18). The valuation method is the price that such property would ordinarily fetch on sale in the open market on the valuation date. No TDS obligation arises as the recipient is outside India. Under s.439(8), a disclosed position must be bona fide and all material facts must be disclosed.
attacked.attack: The provision s.115BBH does not directly address the classification of receipts in USDC as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset. Moreover, the valuation method described is not explicitly mandated by any provision for the valuation of virtual digital assets.
attacked.evidence: Section 115BBH, Income-tax Act, 1961 — carried into the Income-tax Act, 2025: 'Where the total income of an assessee includes any income from the transfer of any virtual digital asset...' Rule 57, Income-tax Rules, 2026: 'The price that such property would ordinarily fetch on sale in the open market on the valuation date.' Neither provision specifies USDC or the valuation method for receipts in USDC.
